completion_gate: baseline_map.md separates, per round count in 3-7, the known attack families and their recalled best-known parameters, with every recalled number explicitly marked unverified_from_memory and no number presented as read from a source.

Every candidate in candidate_report.yaml names its tracked object, the round count at which the object is asserted to hold, explicit assumptions, a concrete prediction, a full end-to-end cost boundary, and its deduplication verdict against each of the six named attack families.
Every candidate records its lossy-projection test outcome, dominated_by, and a quantitative sota_delta.

Every candidate names exactly ONE cheap falsification gate that is runnable inside the local resource envelope and the campaign budget, with its expected wall-clock cost and its required null-object control stated together.

The session may instead return NO_ADMISSIBLE_NEXT_MECHANISM -- that is an admissible and complete outcome -- provided it names the residual open question, states which object classes remain unexamined, and meets the section 4 closure standard rather than reporting a screening count.
constraints: Object-first: every candidate NAMES the concrete mathematical object it tracks through the computation, at a specific round count. 'Attack AES' is not a candidate and must be rejected by the session itself.

Declare the established families off-limits as the primary lens and deduplicate every candidate against them explicitly: integral/square, impossible differential, meet-in-the-middle / Demirci-Selcuk, boomerang, biclique, division property. A candidate that is a renamed variant of one of these is recorded as a rediscovery, not as a candidate.
Apply the lossy-projection test before proposing any experiment: a projection that discards nothing is a change of coordinates, not a new object. Record the test outcome per candidate.
Reduced-round scope only (3-7 rounds). No candidate, phrasing, or extrapolation may assert anything about full-round AES or deployed AES security.
The AES specification is treated as pinned by locally reproducible FIPS-197 known-answer vectors (TASK-20260731-602), not by any read document.

Every literature baseline number cited (biclique key recovery on full AES-128, impossible-differential and meet-in-the-middle results on 7-round AES, integral/square attacks on 4-6 rounds, partial sums) is UNVERIFIED-FROM-MEMORY under this network policy: csrc.nist.gov, eprint.iacr.org, arxiv.org, faest.info and ietf.org are all blocked. Mark each such number 'unverified_from_memory' inline. Presenting a recalled number as if it had been read is a fabrication under AGENTS.md rule 9.

Premature closure is a failure mode symmetric with overclaiming: do not decline to generate on the grounds that AES is exhaustively studied. A closure must meet the docs/inventor-protocol.md section 4 standard -- named obstruction, argument, forward guidance -- and a count of screened-and-rejected mechanisms is a fatigue report, not a closure.

Every candidate carries dominated_by and a quantitative sota_delta. dominated_by: null is permitted only after checking every frontier row across time, memory, and data/queries; an unchecked null is a fabrication.
Charge full end-to-end cost: data complexity, time, memory, precomputation, and verification, at the same round count as the named baseline.

Local resource envelope for any proposed gate: 4 CPU cores, 15 GB RAM, no GPU, no sage; gcc 13.3.0 with -maes, python3 with pycryptodome 3.23.0, openssl CLI. A gate that does not fit must say so rather than be estimated.
Academic defensive cryptanalysis only. Propose no hypothesis status, approve no experiment, and change no official state.
Write only under the assigned task directory.

completion_gate: aes_reduced.py implements AES with a parameterisable round count, and its full-round output for AES-128/192/256 matches the FIPS-197 known-answer vectors.

vector_check_receipt.json is machine-readable and records, per vector: key size, direction, input, expected output, the output from aes_reduced.py, the output from pycryptodome, the output from the openssl CLI, and a pass/fail verdict per comparison.
The receipt records the exact commands, exit statuses, resolved tool versions (python3, pycryptodome, openssl, gcc), the git commit and dirty-tree state, seeds, and timestamps.
The reduced-round convention (which final-round transformations are kept at r < full) is stated explicitly in run_record.md, because every later reduced-round claim depends on it.

run_record.md states the terminal status of every attempted check, including any that failed or did not run, with the reason. No check is reported as passing unless it was executed and its output recorded in the receipt.
constraints: This is an implementation and verification task only. Record observations; make no cryptanalytic claim, propose no mechanism, and change no official state.

The implementation must expose the round count as a parameter (at minimum 3-10 rounds for AES-128) while its full-round behaviour is exactly FIPS-197 AES. Reduced-round variants must document precisely which final-round transformations are kept or dropped, since that convention determines every later result.
Agreement must be demonstrated against BOTH pycryptodome and the openssl CLI independently. Two checks against the same backend do not count as independent agreement.
The implementation under test must not call pycryptodome or openssl internally for the checked path: agreement is only meaningful if the code paths are independent.
Cover all three key sizes (128/192/256) for the full-round known-answer checks, and include both encryption and decryption directions where the reference tools permit.
All randomness is seeded deterministically and every seed is recorded. Any later cryptanalytic run must be reproducible from the receipt.

Record the exact commands run, their exit status, the resolved tool versions, and any check that did NOT run and why. Do not fabricate a command, a version string, an output, or a passing check. A vector that cannot be checked is recorded as unchecked.
The recalled literature is irrelevant to this task: nothing here depends on any unverified baseline number.

If openssl or pycryptodome cannot perform a required check, report it as an infrastructure limitation with the exact failure -- that is a task-scope result, never negative evidence about anything mathematical (AGENTS.md rule 5).
Write only under the assigned task directory.
inputs: GOAL-AES-001 and RQ-AES-001, which make this pinning a hard gate before any cryptanalytic work

handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether this environment can produce an AES ground truth that is pinned locally rather than trusted -- i.e. whether every later reduced-round measurement in this campaign can be certified against an implementation whose correctness was independently demonstrated, without any network access to the specification.
